title: Responsive Web Design
subtitle: Make websites adapt beautifully to phones, tablets and desktops.
description: Learn media queries, responsive units, flexible layouts and mobile-first techniques for modern websites.

blocks.text: Welcome to Lesson 8: Responsive Web Design. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “Responsive Web Design”. The goal is to make websites adapt beautifully to phones, tablets and desktops.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.

Responsive design lets content adapt to the available viewport instead of assuming a single screen size. Flexible widths, min/max constraints, responsive images, and relative units are often more robust than many fixed pixel measurements.

blocks.question: A site works at 390px but overflows at 320px. What is the best next step?
options: Test narrow widths and find the element exceeding its container.
Add one fixed width to body.
blocks.explanation: Responsive testing should include narrower viewports and identify the specific overflow source.

blocks.question: Which is the strongest reason to add a media query?
options: A device is called a tablet.
The CSS file has more than 100 lines.
The content no longer fits well and needs a layout change at that width.
blocks.explanation: Breakpoints should respond to the content’s needs rather than arbitrary device labels.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Breakpoints should respond to the content’s needs rather than arbitrary device labels.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Breakpoints should respond to the content’s needs rather than arbitrary device labels.

blocks.text: Media queries are best added when the content needs a layout change, not merely because a device has a particular name. Start with the narrow layout when appropriate, then enhance it as more space becomes available.

blocks.question: Two validation rules must both pass before submission. Which logical structure is appropriate?
